note: Judgement file for Gate 2 (Episode 1). Never overwritten by tools/gate2-bundle.mjs; open BLOCKERs are read by tools/verify-map.mjs. A01-A22 are the findings of the first independent adversarial audit (review/gate-2/audit/, code f79bf59); R01-R15 are the findings of the second, focused audit of the repairs (review/gate-2/reaudit/, code 07f456e); G2-U* are the author's own unverified/open items. "fixed" means fixed in mechanism AND guarded by a test or gate that was shown to fail on the unrepaired code. 2026-10-05: the owner approved Gate 2 as APPROVE DIRECTION with two limited revisions (hit volumes match the visible enemy, PT-005; a focused outline-readability pass). Items A04, A09, A13, A14, R14, A21 (M12) and the real-GPU measurement are DEFERRED by that decision unless an actual player-facing problem makes one necessary (REPAIR_PLAN.md WP3-WP9).

defects.title: M07 and M08 exits were never locked (two exit entities on one cell; the unlocked one won)
defects.how: The duplicate '>' glyphs are gone. validateMap now rejects two exits on one cell, a locked exit nothing can unlock, and a switch that needs an item the level lacks. tests/kit.test.js pins all three, plus the shipped M05/M07/M08 being gated.

defects.title: No check that a level cannot be finished without its designed gate
defects.how: viability.js gateSkip(): a fighting bot sent straight at each main exit must not complete the level; runs in verify-map and in the generic per-map test; a test proves the probe catches an exit whose lock does not lock. validateMap also rejects a sector no switch or trigger ever moves.
defects.remaining: reach.js is still optimistic about switches, sectors and locks (it says so); the probe and the canonical route are what prove gating.

defects.title: Warden knockback tunnelled through walls (end-point-only collision)
defects.how: tryMove moves in steps of at most 0.25 m and stops at the wall; test: a 3 m shove and a real Warden charge beside a wall never cross it.

defects.title: Bot-tuned maps had almost no margin for a weaker player
defects.how: Every map now needs rounds available >= 1.5x what the perfect bot fires (M07 and M08 gained ammo, M06 gained ammo on its route); a strafing fighter with 0.03 rad aim error, and one whose ammo pickups are worth 25% less, must complete every map on normal (viability gate); a last-resort flare feed means a player with no ammunition of any kind is never left without a weapon.
defects.remaining: Hard difficulty is still fragile when the player is degraded (M06 hard with both handicaps kills the strafing bot). Per-type ammo slack is now gated (>= 1.5x per ammunition type the bot fires >= 5 times) and M08 hard now completes on 8 of 8 seeds (it was 4 of 8). Nobody human has played it (G2-U1). 2026-10-05: M08 hard completes on 52 of 64 seeds (81%) for the perfect bot, before AND after the fairer hit volumes; the carried Episode 1 hard test now needs 2 of 3 seeds, the same policy as the per-map hard gate.

defects.title: Stale and inconsistent documentation (TESTING.md still reported Gate 1 numbers)
defects.how: TESTING.md, PRODUCTION_LOG.md, README table refreshed from the final evidence.
defects.remaining: Docs were refreshed twice from evidence; small drift keeps reappearing where numbers are typed by hand (see R12). The bundle README is generated; TESTING.md is not.

defects.title: validateMap threw on malformed shapes and accepted nonsense values
defects.how: validateMap wraps its checks (never throws), refuses maps over 400 per side or 25,600 cells, and range-checks cellSize, ceilingHeight and quality; test covers ten malformed shapes. The audit fuzz script now reports 0 throws, 0 hangs.

defects.title: Resuming a save was not identical to uninterrupted play (nav-field cache history)
defects.how: Distance fields are keyed by the target cell AND a version of everything they depend on (door passability, sector heights), not by age; test: save/load mid-run on M05 with awake enemies gives an identical state hash.

defects.title: Broken saves could throw or freeze the shell
defects.how: loadWorld checks the saved world's structure (missing/mistyped fields, non-finite numbers, unknown enemy kinds, door/sector counts) and returns a reason; the shell guards loadWorld and falls through to the next slot.
defects.remaining: A null in a required field is now rejected and a crash inside the sim step drops to the title with a reason; a save that is structurally valid but semantically wrong (another map's world inside a save, an unknown sector id) can still load.

defects.title: The render-budget baseline check was vacuous for the Gate 2 vantage points (baseline recorded from the same run) and the awake ceiling was set just above the measured maximum
defects.remaining: The baseline is now recorded once (at the Gate 2 evidence run) and compares from then on; the 900-call awake-crowd ceiling is an engineering budget, not a measurement (see G2-U3).

defects.title: AGENT_VERIFIED survived engine changes
defects.how: Evidence carries a hash of src/engine/*.js; npm run validate downgrades any map whose evidence was produced by other engine code (test in campaign.test.js).

defects.title: M05's funicular was optional
defects.how: The east stairs between terraces one and two are gone: the car is the only way up (a call lever at its foot brings it back down); the lever on the car rides with it (A22).

defects.title: Sky texture seam, dark secret-level horizon, mislabelled or in-collider screenshots
defects.how: Skies are cross-faded into a horizontally periodic texture at load; M08 chamber views were re-taken from clear positions and every tour was regenerated.
defects.remaining: The sea beyond the Lighthouse Cellar and the hill's outer wall is still a near-black horizon band (dark water under a dark fog); not judged by a person.

defects.title: Repository hygiene: ~117 MB of tracked review images, loose git objects
defects.how: git gc run (no history rewrite).
defects.remaining: review/ still holds the screenshot tours twice (per-map folders and the gate bundle copies); prune or LFS them before the repository grows further.

defects.title: Explosion splash ignores walls and cover (flares hurt and wake enemies through walls)
defects.remaining: Not fixed: changing splash rules re-tunes every map and the Warden's plate design assumes splash gets through; needs a design decision (line of sight from the blast, not from the projectile).

defects.title: The objective panel covered the Cantor's health bar
defects.how: The objective line moves below the boss bar while a boss is awake.
defects.remaining: Stacked toasts can still cover the middle of the screen in a busy fight.

defects.title: Balance evidence started each map cold but the game carries inventory between maps
defects.how: Arrival inventory is the carried one FLOORED at the map's authored loadout (health, each ammo type, weapons): the cold-start evidence is a lower bound on every arrival, and nobody starts a map at 1 HP with an empty gun. tests/chain.test.js plays M01->M08 carried on hard (seed 2, the audit's failing case) and on normal.

defects.title: New Game restarted the last-played map
defects.how: New Game and the default of startLevel are C1E1M01; the browser check plays a map, quits, clicks a difficulty and asserts C1E1M01.

defects.title: Continue loaded the quick-save even when the auto-save was newer
defects.how: Continue loads the newest readable slot by savedAt and falls through on a corrupt one; the browser check asserts it.

defects.title: canonicalRoute.expectedEvents was a hard-coded, never-checked constant
defects.how: Removed from the evidence.

defects.title: M05 taught a lamp-signal system that does not exist; brief items undelivered
defects.how: M05's text no longer promises signalling lamps; design/EPISODE1.md has an 'As built' section listing what was dropped or changed (lamp signals, trap drops, M08's rising platforms).

defects.title: Test-suite weaknesses (vacuous assertions, audio coverage not reading script.js, 8 of 22 surviving mutations)
defects.how: The two vacuous assertions are real assertions; the audio coverage test scans every src/engine file; new pinned-number tests cover the Warden plate/stun/knockback, pulse damage, armour, the dead:<group> rule and the seal action (the mutations M11, M13, M14, M18, M19, M20, M21 each now fail a test).
defects.remaining: M12 (melee ignores the height difference) is not pinned by a test. After the second audit the seven surviving mutations were re-checked one by one: M21 (Cantor pulse damage) had still survived and is now pinned to the literal 22; the tryMove and nav guards were mutation-tested (each new test fails on the old code). The full 22-mutation run was not repeated.

defects.title: Pickups and switches on moving floors kept their creation height
defects.how: Pickups follow the floor each tick, switch reach and the panel's drawn height use the floor under the switch; test rides a lever and a pickup up a car.

defects.title: Three repairs were guarded by tests that passed on the unrepaired code (A18 browser check never wrote the quick save; the A03 tests started the player inside the wall / ran the Warden away; the A07 resume test could not see the old cache)
defects.how: The A18 check now writes the quick save with t.save() and asserts it exists; the A03 test starts the player 0.6 m before the wall and fires a real Warden charge eastward at a player 0.55 m from it (asserts an enemy_strike and that the player stays in the near room); the A07 test opens a door while a cached field exists and requires the running world to agree with a fresh one. Each guard was verified by mutating the repaired code back to the old behaviour: the new tests fail (tryMove, nav cache).

defects.title: M21 (Cantor pulse damage) still survived; the robustness/gate glue and navVersion were pinned by nothing
defects.how: The pulse test pins the literal 22 (a pin against the config itself was vacuous; the mutation now fails). tests/viability.test.js turns every viabilityChecks gate red with synthetic evidence, exercises gateSkip on mutated shipped maps, checks ammo bookkeeping per type and proves ammoScale/tremor degrade only the player.

defects.title: The gate-skip probe treated a dead or stuck bot as gated, skipped maps whose enemies all arrive by script, and let quality.safe switch every check off
defects.how: The probe now uses an invulnerable bot with 5 simulated minutes; only a finished level counts as a skipped gate (and a death is not accepted as proof); scripted spawns count as threats; a safe room must really contain no enemies.

defects.title: Exit id schemes disagreed between the validator and MapData
defects.how: One scheme: explicit id, else "exit" + index among all exits; a two-exit test pins it.

defects.title: M05-M08 changed without a version bump, so an old mid-level save kept the old world (including the unlocked exit)
defects.how: M05, M06, M07 and M08 are version 2; a save made against version 1 resumes from the level start.

defects.title: Ammo slack summed unlike ammunition types
defects.how: Slack is gated per type (>= 1.5x for every type the bot fires 5 or more times) as well as in total; M06, M07 and M08 gained pickups to satisfy it.

defects.title: The arrival floor makes carried health meaningless and lets a rich player skip authored scarcity, while docs said "inventory carried"
defects.how: Stated plainly in GAME_VISION.md: every map starts at full health; ammunition and weapons carry over floored at the authored loadout; scarcity is a floor, not a ceiling.
defects.remaining: A design decision worth a human opinion: dying and retrying always restores the arrival loadout, never worse.

defects.title: The last-resort flare feed makes scarcity soft (an unlimited stream of flares completes a map with zero pickups)
defects.how: The feed is slower (one flare per 10 s, only with no ammunition of any kind) so it cannot compete with playing normally.
defects.remaining: It still makes total starvation survivable by an extremely patient player; that is the intent (no soft-lock), recorded here as a known effect.

defects.title: Nav fields were rebuilt every tick while a moving floor moved (19-30x the old cost in a synthetic case)
defects.how: A moving floor is treated as standing at the nearest quarter metre by the navigation field and its version, so a field is rebuilt a few times per metre of travel; still a pure function of state.

defects.title: makeSeamless had no fallback and stretches the sky 12.5% horizontally
defects.how: Any canvas failure keeps the original sky; the stretch is accepted (clouds only).

defects.title: Evidence freshness was weaker than it read (no engine hash = never stale; raw-byte hashes go stale on a CRLF checkout)
defects.how: validate treats evidence without an engine hash as stale, and tools/textsha.mjs hashes text with CRLF folded to LF for map, route, engine and browser-check stamps.

defects.title: Documentation still contradicted the evidence in several places
defects.how: TESTING.md budget/perf/baseline/save-migration lines, GAME_VISION.md length statement, AGENTS.md verify-map description and the bundle sentences corrected; volatile timings now point at the evidence file instead of being copied.

defects.title: A null array field passed the save structure check and then threw in step()
defects.how: Null is accepted only where a fresh world is null too; a crash inside the sim step now drops to the title with a reason.

defects.title: Continue can prefer the auto-save over an older manual quick save (every level entry and Retry rewrites auto)
defects.remaining: Plausible rather than reproduced in a browser: after an F5, dying and pressing Retry rewrites the auto slot with a newer time, so Continue loads the level start of the retry, not the F5. Newest-wins is the documented rule; a save-slot picker would remove the ambiguity.

defects.title: Completion was judged on ONE seed; the perfect bot died on 4 of 8 seeds on Bell Tower hard, and the carried chain died there on hard seeds 3 and 4
defects.how: The viability gate needs all three simulated seeds to finish on easy and normal and two of three on hard; M08 gained armour, health and ammunition (hard now completes 8 of 8 seeds, damage ~180 instead of 200-270); the carried-chain test covers hard seeds 2, 3 and 4 and normal seed 1.

defects.title: Hand play of the nine maps: the owner played Episode 1 (2026-10-05) and reports solid gameplay; per-map and per-difficulty detail was not recorded
defects.remaining: The owner (2026-10-05): played Episode 1, "gameplay is solid", approved the gameplay and visual direction. Not recorded: which of the nine maps, which difficulties, par times, the Cantor fight. Hard difficulty and every par time were still tuned against a bot only.

defects.title: Audio has never been heard by a person
defects.remaining: 54 effects pass the offline measurements (finite, audible, below full scale, decaying) but nobody has listened to them or to the mix; the tone pulse, bell node, ramp, lift, lights-surge and dry-feed sounds are the least certain.

defects.title: Real-GPU performance is unmeasured; crowds are expensive
defects.remaining: Only software-GL numbers exist. Each awake enemy rig is about 30 draw calls; with every enemy awake and in view the market (M03) reaches ~820 and the ferry quay (M06) ~830 draw calls (ceiling 900, an engineering budget). Sleeping enemies are merged, so quiet play is cheap. A rig LOD is the obvious fix if a real GPU disagrees.

defects.title: Pointer lock has never been exercised in a real browser session
defects.remaining: Carried over from Gate 1 (F14). The retry logic exists; the Esc -> Resume -> click flow needs a hand test in real Chrome.

defects.title: Par times are placeholders
defects.remaining: Every par is 2x-8x the bot's time by rule, not from a human run.

defects.title: Enemy and boss models are code-authored variants on one rig, reviewed only in stills
defects.remaining: The Sexton, Warden-Graft and Cantor differ by silhouette (extra meshes), not by animation. Never judged in motion by a person; in the chamber screenshots the Cantor is largely hidden by its own shield wireframe and the cover pillars.

defects.title: The per-map 'damage rises with difficulty' check was a loose proxy
defects.remaining: Per map it is now only easy < normal and easy <= hard; the hard-vs-normal trend is gated over the whole episode by episodeDifficultyChecks (tools/gate2-bundle.mjs). Reason: a deterministic bot takes 2-6 hits per map, so one hit moved M06 from 54 vs 70 to 36 vs 82 while the episode total stayed easy < normal < hard.

defects.title: The bot is the only judge of the boss fight
defects.remaining: The bot takes cover behind pillars from tone pulses and cuts the ring first; a human may find a dominant tactic (high ground, door camping) or an unfair one. The chamber door seals behind the player and only reopens when the Cantor dies.

defects.title: Set dressing repeats; some spaces read as rectangles
defects.remaining: Terrace streets, the quay and the tower legs are long rectangles with props on a grid. Verticality and hazards vary the maps, but the level art is still a kit, not hand-dressed. The Signal House 'beds' are tables.

defects.title: Only Episode 1 exists; C1E2-C2 (59 maps) are not started
defects.remaining: By design: Gate 3 has not been approved.

defects.title: Playtest 2026-09-30: awake enemies drawn UNDER raised floors (C1E1M02 gallery, 3 m) and corpses sunk into the floor
defects.how: Root cause: pose() overwrote the world root height after the view placed it (also: death/crouch buried the mesh, scale on the root mis-placed sleeping Wardens/Sextons/Cantor, dead/stunned enemies ignored moving floors). Fixed by splitting world root from pose rig + a contact solver; guarded by tests/rig-grounding, enemy-hit-volume, sim-sector-ground and the render-truth census in the browser gate (2/8 census checks passed on the old code, 0 violations now).
defects.remaining: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER IN PLAY 2026-10-05 ("my issues were resolved and gameplay is solid"). Still not asserted by any check: that the drawn floor surface equals the sim floor; pickups on moving decks (REPAIR_PLAN.md WP2).

defects.title: Playtest 2026-09-30: same symptom in C1E1M04 (the raised shop, 2 m)
defects.how: Same causes and guards as PT-001.
defects.remaining: CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER IN PLAY 2026-10-05.

defects.title: Rivet pickup toast said +30 while the pickup grants 40; debris used world y = 0 as the floor; the 800x600 pause control list was clipped against the Reset button
defects.how: Toast amounts derive from PICKUPS (tests/pickup-toasts + a real-game browser check); debris lands on the terrain under it (tests/debris-floor + a browser check over the 3 m gallery); the nested scroller is gone and the browser check measures four window sizes.

defects.title: Evidence freshness covered only src/engine; assetVersion was recorded and never checked; only the main route was hashed; a bundle could claim 9 AGENT_VERIFIED while the derived status was 0 (the old validate printed OK for exactly that at 8dc307c)
defects.how: tools/textsha.mjs source sets + dependency table; evidence records `sources`; validate marks stale on engine/render/game/audio/asset/map/ANY-route changes and on a browser check without the census; validate fails when a live bundle contradicts the derived status; tests/freshness.test.js (9 of 13 fail on the old validator).
defects.remaining: Numbers typed by hand in TESTING.md / PRODUCTION_LOG.md / GAME_VISION.md prose are still unguarded.

defects.title: Rendered bodies are taller than their sim hit cylinders: Cantor 4.79 m drawn vs 3.2 m hit, Warden 3.00 vs 2.3, Sexton 2.37 vs 1.85, Bellhand 2.37 vs 1.9, Tollbearer 2.26 vs 1.95 (Gaunt and Bell node match)
defects.remaining: FIXED IN CODE, NOT CONFIRMED BY THE OWNER IN PLAY. Attack poses are not fitted (the standing rig is the reference); arms, weapons and trailing cloth past the torso are deliberately not hittable.
defects.how: Owner decision 2026-10-05 (the hit box must match the enemy). src/engine/hitvolume.js: heights = the drawn heights, hitRadius/hitForward for the Cantor and the Gaunt, flares burst on the body, splash is measured from the blast height. Guarded by tests/hit-volume-fair.test.js (4 of 6 fail on the old numbers; over-tall and over-wide mutations fail) and a census check in the real game.

defects.title: Outline readability pass (owner revision 2, 2026-10-05): made, appearance only
defects.how: src/render/post.js: crease detection (absolute second difference of 1/z), lower silhouette thresholds, less broken ink. Before/after of 12 fixed viewpoints and ink masks in review/outlines/ (ink share 3.3% -> 7.0%).
defects.remaining: Nobody has judged whether it reads better or is too heavy. A dark Gaunt on a dark wall is still dark on dark (palette, not outline). The Outline setting still turns the pass off.
